context:
Goal: settle Card in Hand's open choices, so Duo can plan the build.
Problem: we don't know if the iPhone keyboard fits inside one page of the open Duo (case A) or spans both (case B). Case A needs nothing. This is only for case B.
New at 14:06: the fold run measured the keyboard frame at 951 x 263 pt on the open inner screen. That's the full width, so it spans the fold: case B (measured). The keys themselves didn't show in the screenshots, so this rests on the frame size alone.
Based on: decision duo-card-in-hand, your 12:25 picks (ruling); the fold and keyboard are unmeasured (measured: the runs failed at load 157).
Meanwhile: Duo plans the build and starts nothing until you answer.

designs.label: Case A for reference: keys fit the left page
b) System keys across both pages (B2)

holds: Duo's build plan for Card in Hand waits on this.

options.gain: The keys stay on the left page, and the answer stays visible on the right.
options.how: Our own keys on the left page, with a System keys switch to the real keyboard.
options.label: In-app key pad (B1)
options.lose: No autocorrect, dictation or swipe typing; keys are 42pt, under the 44pt floor.

options.how: Use the real keyboard; the query moves down onto it.
options.label: System keys across both pages (B2)
options.lose: The right page keeps only 3 lines.

ref: Duo design round 2, draft PR #144 (Card in Hand screens)
title: If the keyboard spans the fold, which keys does Card in Hand use?
why: The answer page stays readable. Build for case A first, since it's the likely one.
